910.name: Illyrian Tribes and Ancient Albania
910.description: The Illyrian tribal confederations that inhabited the western Balkans, their culture, warfare, and eventual subjugation by the Roman Republic following the Illyrian Wars.

sub_clusters.name: Illyrian Tribal Kingdoms
sub_clusters.description: Early Illyrian tribal societies including the Taulantii, Ardiaei, and Dardani, their settlements, and interactions with Greek colonies along the coast.

sub_clusters.name: Illyrian Wars and Roman Conquest
sub_clusters.description: The three Illyrian Wars fought between Rome and the Illyrian kingdoms, culminating in the defeat of King Gentius and the absorption of Illyria into the Roman sphere.
key_events: First Illyrian War against Queen Teuta (229–228 BC)
Defeat of King Gentius and end of Illyrian independence (168 BC)

910.name: Roman Illyria and Via Egnatia
910.description: Roman provincial administration of Illyria, construction of the Via Egnatia connecting Rome to Byzantium, and the spread of Christianity in the Albanian lands.

sub_clusters.name: Via Egnatia and Romanization
sub_clusters.description: Construction and significance of the Via Egnatia as a vital military and trade route through Albanian territory, and the cultural Romanization of Illyrian society.

sub_clusters.name: Early Christianity in Illyria
sub_clusters.description: The spread of Christianity through Roman Illyria, the establishment of early bishoprics, and the division between Rome and Constantinople that would shape Albania's religious landscape.

920.name: Byzantine and Medieval Albania
920.description: Albanian lands under Byzantine rule, Slavic migrations, Bulgarian incursions, and the emergence of distinct Albanian identity through the medieval period.

sub_clusters.name: Byzantine Rule and Slavic Migrations
sub_clusters.description: The impact of Slavic migrations on the Albanian-speaking population, Byzantine administrative control, and the preservation of Albanian identity in mountainous regions.

sub_clusters.name: Bulgarian and Serbian Domination
sub_clusters.description: Periods of Bulgarian Empire and later Serbian Empire control over Albanian territories, shifting allegiances, and the Arbër principalities.

920.name: Albanian Principalities and Skanderbeg
920.description: The rise of Albanian feudal principalities, the legendary resistance of Gjergj Kastrioti Skanderbeg against the Ottoman Empire, and the eventual fall of Albania to Ottoman rule.

sub_clusters.name: Principality of Arbër and Feudal Lords
sub_clusters.description: The Principality of Arbër as the first Albanian state, the Thopia, Kastrioti, and Muzaka noble families, and competing influences of Venice, Naples, and Serbia.

sub_clusters.name: Skanderbeg's Resistance to the Ottomans
sub_clusters.description: Gjergj Kastrioti Skanderbeg's 25-year military campaign against the Ottoman Empire, the League of Lezhë, and his status as Albania's national hero.
key_events: Skanderbeg raises Albanian revolt and the League of Lezhë is formed (1444)
Death of Skanderbeg; Albanian resistance continues briefly (1468)

sub_clusters.name: Fall of Albania to the Ottomans
sub_clusters.description: The collapse of Albanian resistance after Skanderbeg's death, Ottoman conquest of the remaining fortresses, and the beginning of five centuries of Ottoman rule.

930.name: Ottoman Albania — Early Period
930.description: The first two centuries of Ottoman rule in Albania, mass conversion to Islam, Albanian soldiers and administrators in Ottoman service, and the transformation of Albanian society.

sub_clusters.name: Islamization of Albania
sub_clusters.description: The gradual conversion of a majority of Albanians to Islam, creating a unique religious mosaic of Muslim, Orthodox, and Catholic communities that persists today.

sub_clusters.name: Albanians in Ottoman Service
sub_clusters.description: The prominence of ethnic Albanians in the Ottoman military and bureaucracy, including numerous grand viziers of Albanian origin and the devshirme system.

940.name: Ottoman Albania — Late Period and Albanian Renaissance
940.description: The decline of Ottoman central authority, autonomous Albanian pashaliks, the Albanian National Awakening (Rilindja), and the movement toward independence.

sub_clusters.name: Albanian Pashaliks and Autonomy
sub_clusters.description: The rise of powerful semi-autonomous Albanian rulers like Ali Pasha of Ioannina and the Bushati family, who governed vast territories with near-independence from Istanbul.

sub_clusters.name: Albanian National Awakening (Rilindja)
sub_clusters.description: The Albanian Renaissance movement: the standardization of the Albanian language, the League of Prizren (1878), cultural and political mobilization, and the struggle for national identity.
key_events: League of Prizren formed to defend Albanian-inhabited lands (1878)
Congress of Monastir standardizes the Albanian alphabet (1908)

sub_clusters.name: Declaration of Independence (1912)
sub_clusters.description: Ismail Qemali's declaration of Albanian independence in Vlorë on November 28, 1912, international recognition at the London Conference, and the creation of the Principality of Albania.

950.name: Interwar Albania and Zog Monarchy
950.description: Albania's turbulent interwar period: foreign occupation during WWI, the Republic of Mirdita, Fan Noli's government, and Ahmet Zog's transformation from president to self-declared king.

sub_clusters.name: WWI Occupation and Early Republic
sub_clusters.description: Foreign occupation during WWI, the Congress of Lushnjë, Fan Noli's democratic revolution of 1924, and its overthrow by Ahmet Zog.

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Zog
sub_clusters.description: Ahmet Zog's self-proclamation as King Zog I, Italian economic penetration, modernization efforts, and the growing dependence on Mussolini's Italy.

950.name: WWII and Hoxha Communist Regime
950.description: Italian and German occupation during WWII, the communist partisan movement led by Enver Hoxha, and four decades of hardline Stalinist isolation that made Albania the most closed society in Europe.

sub_clusters.name: Italian and German Occupation (WWII)
sub_clusters.description: Italian annexation of Albania in 1939, the failed Italian invasion of Greece from Albanian soil, German occupation, and the rise of communist partisans under Enver Hoxha.

sub_clusters.name: Hoxha's Stalinist Isolationism
sub_clusters.description: Enver Hoxha's totalitarian communist state: breaks with Yugoslavia, the Soviet Union, and China; the campaign of atheism; construction of 750,000 bunkers; and extreme international isolation.
key_events: Albania declared the world's first atheist state (1967)
Construction of approximately 750,000 concrete bunkers across the country (1967–1985)

sub_clusters.name: Collapse of Communism
sub_clusters.description: The death of Hoxha, Ramiz Alia's cautious reforms, student protests, the fall of the communist regime, and Albania's painful emergence from isolation.

960.name: Post-Communist Albania and European Integration
960.description: Albania's chaotic transition to democracy and market economy, the devastating 1997 pyramid scheme crisis, NATO membership, and the ongoing EU accession process.

sub_clusters.name: Transition and Pyramid Scheme Crisis
sub_clusters.description: The turbulent 1990s: economic collapse, mass emigration, the 1997 collapse of pyramid schemes that wiped out citizens' savings, armed insurrection, and international intervention.
key_events: Collapse of pyramid schemes triggers armed insurrection and near state failure (1997)

sub_clusters.name: NATO Membership and EU Candidacy
sub_clusters.description: Albania's accession to NATO in 2009, granting of EU candidate status in 2014, ongoing reforms in judiciary and governance, and the long road toward European integration.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
